name: A
doc: Make \w, \W, \b, \B, \d, \D, \s and \S perform ASCII-only matching instead of full Unicode matching. This is only meaningful for Unicode (str) patterns, and is ignored for bytes patterns.

name: ASCII
doc: Make \w, \W, \b, \B, \d, \D, \s and \S perform ASCII-only matching instead of full Unicode matching. This is only meaningful for Unicode (str) patterns, and is ignored for bytes patterns.

name: compile
doc: Compile a regular expression pattern, returning a Pattern object.

name: DEBUG
doc: Display debug information about compiled expression.

name: DOTALL
doc: Make the '.' special character match any character at all, including a newline; without this flag, '.' will match anything except a newline.

name: escape
doc: Escape special characters in a string.

changed.text: The '_' character is no longer escaped.
Only characters that can have special meaning in a regular expression are escaped. As a result, '!', '"', '%', "'", ',', '/', ':', ';', '<', '=', '>', '@', and "`" are no longer escaped.

name: findall
doc:
Return a list of all non-overlapping matches in the string.

If one or more capturing groups are present in the pattern, return
a list of groups; this will be a list of tuples if the pattern
has more than one group.

Empty matches are included in the result.

changed.text: Non-empty matches can now start just after a previous empty match.

name: finditer
doc:
Return an iterator over all non-overlapping matches in the
string.  For each match, the iterator returns a Match object.

Empty matches are included in the result.

changed.text: Non-empty matches can now start just after a previous empty match.

name: fullmatch
doc:
Try to apply the pattern to all of the string, returning
a Match object, or None if no match was found.

name: I
doc: Perform case-insensitive matching; expressions like [A-Z] will also match lowercase letters. Full Unicode matching (such as Ü matching ü) also works unless the ASCII flag is used to disable non-ASCII matches. The current locale does not change the effect of this flag unless the LOCALE flag is also used.

name: IGNORECASE
doc: Perform case-insensitive matching; expressions like [A-Z] will also match lowercase letters. Full Unicode matching (such as Ü matching ü) also works unless the ASCII flag is used to disable non-ASCII matches. The current locale does not change the effect of this flag unless the LOCALE flag is also used.

name: L
doc: Make \w, \W, \b, \B and case-insensitive matching dependent on the current locale. This flag can be used only with bytes patterns.

changed.text: LOCALE can be used only with bytes patterns and is not compatible with ASCII.
Compiled regular expression objects with the LOCALE flag no longer depend on the locale at compile time. Only the locale at matching time affects the result of matching.

name: LOCALE
doc: Make \w, \W, \b, \B and case-insensitive matching dependent on the current locale. This flag can be used only with bytes patterns.

changed.text: LOCALE can be used only with bytes patterns and is not compatible with ASCII.
Compiled regular expression objects with the LOCALE flag no longer depend on the locale at compile time. Only the locale at matching time affects the result of matching.

name: M
doc: When specified, the pattern character '^' matches at the beginning of the string and at the beginning of each line (immediately following each newline); and the pattern character '$' matches at the end of the string and at the end of each line (immediately preceding each newline). By default, '^' matches only at the beginning of the string, and '$' only at the end of the string and immediately before the newline (if any) at the end of the string.

name: Match
doc:
The result of re.search(), re.prefixmatch(), and re.fullmatch().
Match objects always have a boolean value of True.

changed.text: re.Match supports [] to indicate a Unicode (str) or bytes match. See Generic Alias Type.

name: match
doc:
Try to apply the pattern at the start of the string, returning
a Match object, or None if no match was found.

changed.text: Soft deprecated. match() has been soft deprecated in favor of the alternate prefixmatch() name of this API which is more explicitly descriptive. Use it to better express intent. The norm in other languages and regular expression implementations is to use the term match to refer to the behavior of what Python has always called search(). See prefixmatch() vs. match().

name: __getitem__
doc: Return self[key].

name: end
doc: Return index of the end of the substring matched by group.

name: endpos
doc: The index into the string beyond which the RE engine will not go.

name: expand
doc: Return the string obtained by doing backslash substitution on the string template, as done by the sub() method.

changed.text: Unmatched groups are replaced with an empty string.

name: group
doc:
group([group1, ...]) -> str or tuple.
Return subgroup(s) of the match by indices or names.
For 0 returns the entire match.

name: groupdict
doc:
Return a dictionary containing all the named subgroups of the match, keyed by the subgroup name.

default
  Is used for groups that did not participate in the match.

name: groups
doc:
Return a tuple containing all the subgroups of the match, from 1.

default
  Is used for groups that did not participate in the match.

name: lastgroup
doc: The name of the last matched capturing group.

name: lastindex
doc: The integer index of the last matched capturing group.

name: pos
doc: The index into the string at which the RE engine started looking for a match.

name: re
doc: The regular expression object.

name: span
doc: For match object m, return the 2-tuple (m.start(group), m.end(group)).

name: start
doc: Return index of the start of the substring matched by group.

name: string
doc: The string passed to match() or search().

name: MULTILINE
doc: When specified, the pattern character '^' matches at the beginning of the string and at the beginning of each line (immediately following each newline); and the pattern character '$' matches at the end of the string and at the end of each line (immediately preceding each newline). By default, '^' matches only at the beginning of the string, and '$' only at the end of the string and immediately before the newline (if any) at the end of the string.

name: NOFLAG
doc: Indicates no flag being applied, the value is 0. This flag may be used as a default value for a function keyword argument or as a base value that will be conditionally ORed with other flags. Example of use as a default value:

name: Pattern
doc: Compiled regular expression object.

changed.text: re.Pattern supports [] to indicate a Unicode (str) or bytes pattern. See Generic Alias Type.

name: findall
doc: Return a list of all non-overlapping matches of pattern in string.

name: finditer
doc:
Return an iterator over all non-overlapping matches for the RE pattern in string.

For each match, the iterator returns a match object.

name: flags
doc: The regex matching flags.

name: fullmatch
doc: Matches against all of the string.

name: groupindex
doc: A dictionary mapping group names to group numbers.

name: groups
doc: The number of capturing groups in the pattern.

name: match
doc:
prefixmatch($self, /, string, pos=0, endpos=sys.maxsize)
--

Matches zero or more characters at the beginning of the string.

changed.text: Soft deprecated. match() has been soft deprecated in favor of the alternate prefixmatch() name of this API which is more explicitly descriptive. Use it to better express intent. The norm in other languages and regular expression implementations is to use the term match to refer to the behavior of what Python has always called search(). See prefixmatch() vs. match().

name: pattern
doc: The pattern string from which the RE object was compiled.

name: prefixmatch
doc: Matches zero or more characters at the beginning of the string.

name: search
doc:
Scan through string looking for a match, and return a corresponding match object instance.

Return None if no position in the string matches.

name: split
doc: Split string by the occurrences of pattern.

name: sub
doc: Return the string obtained by replacing the leftmost non-overlapping occurrences of pattern in string by the replacement repl.

name: subn
doc: Return the tuple (new_string, number_of_subs_made) found by replacing the leftmost non-overlapping occurrences of pattern with the replacement repl.

name: PatternError
doc:
Exception raised for invalid regular expressions.

Attributes:

    msg: The unformatted error message
    pattern: The regular expression pattern
    pos: The index in the pattern where compilation failed (may be None)
    lineno: The line corresponding to pos (may be None)
    colno: The column corresponding to pos (may be None)

changed.text: Added additional attributes.
PatternError was originally named error; the latter is kept as an alias for backward compatibility.

name: colno
doc: The column corresponding to pos (may be None).

name: lineno
doc: The line corresponding to pos (may be None).

name: msg
doc: The unformatted error message.

name: pattern
doc: The regular expression pattern.

name: pos
doc: The index in pattern where compilation failed (may be None).

name: prefixmatch
doc:
Try to apply the pattern at the start of the string, returning
a Match object, or None if no match was found.

name: purge
doc: Clear the regular expression caches

name: RegexFlag
doc: An enumeration.

name: S
doc: Make the '.' special character match any character at all, including a newline; without this flag, '.' will match anything except a newline.

name: search
doc:
Scan through string looking for a match to the pattern, returning
a Match object, or None if no match was found.

name: split
doc:
Split the source string by the occurrences of the pattern,
returning a list containing the resulting substrings.  If
capturing parentheses are used in pattern, then the text of all
groups in the pattern are also returned as part of the resulting
list.  If maxsplit is nonzero, at most maxsplit splits occur,
and the remainder of the string is returned as the final element
of the list.

changed.text: Added the optional flags argument.
Added support of splitting on a pattern that could match an empty string.

deprecated.text: Passing maxsplit and flags as positional arguments is deprecated. In future Python versions they will be keyword-only parameters.

name: sub
doc:
Return the string obtained by replacing the leftmost
non-overlapping occurrences of the pattern in string by the
replacement repl.  repl can be either a string or a callable;
if a string, backslash escapes in it are processed.  If it is
a callable, it's passed the Match object and must return
a replacement string to be used.

changed.text: Added the optional flags argument.
Unmatched groups are replaced with an empty string.
Unknown escapes in pattern consisting of '\' and an ASCII letter now are errors.
Unknown escapes in repl consisting of '\' and an ASCII letter now are errors. An empty match can occur immediately after a non-empty match.
Group id can only contain ASCII digits. In bytes replacement strings, group name can only contain bytes in the ASCII range (b'\x00'-b'\x7f').

deprecated.text: Passing count and flags as positional arguments is deprecated. In future Python versions they will be keyword-only parameters.

name: subn
doc:
Return a 2-tuple containing (new_string, number).
new_string is the string obtained by replacing the leftmost
non-overlapping occurrences of the pattern in the source
string by the replacement repl.  number is the number of
substitutions that were made. repl can be either a string or a
callable; if a string, backslash escapes in it are processed.
If it is a callable, it's passed the Match object and must
return a replacement string to be used.

name: U
doc: In Python 3, Unicode characters are matched by default for str patterns. This flag is therefore redundant with no effect and is only kept for backward compatibility.

name: UNICODE
doc: In Python 3, Unicode characters are matched by default for str patterns. This flag is therefore redundant with no effect and is only kept for backward compatibility.

name: VERBOSE
doc: This flag allows you to write regular expressions that look nicer and are more readable by allowing you to visually separate logical sections of the pattern and add comments. Whitespace within the pattern is ignored, except when in a character class, or when preceded by an unescaped backslash, or within tokens like *?, (?: or (?P<...>. For example, (? : and * ? are not allowed. When a line contains a # that is not in a character class and is not preceded by an unescaped backslash, all characters from the leftmost such # through the end of the line are ignored.

name: X
doc: This flag allows you to write regular expressions that look nicer and are more readable by allowing you to visually separate logical sections of the pattern and add comments. Whitespace within the pattern is ignored, except when in a character class, or when preceded by an unescaped backslash, or within tokens like *?, (?: or (?P<...>. For example, (? : and * ? are not allowed. When a line contains a # that is not in a character class and is not preceded by an unescaped backslash, all characters from the leftmost such # through the end of the line are ignored.
